category_title: Young child with severe autism engaging in physical aggression
minimal_context: Lauren is seated at a table in her classroom with toys to play with independently while the teacher reads some papers.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here are your toys, Lauren. I am going to read these papers now, so you need to play by yourself.

STUDENT: (Pushes the toys aside) Play.

TUTOR: I have to finish reading this right now. Keep playing with your toys.

STUDENT: (Stands up and grabs the teacher's arm) Look!

TUTOR: Lauren, please sit back down in your chair.

STUDENT: (Screams loudly, kicks the teacher's leg, and grabs the teacher's clothing, pulling hard) No!

options.A: Turn toward the student and issue a statement of concern, such as “What do you need?” along with brief physical contact.
options.B: Provide the student with digital apps that feature instant rewards with audio and text during independent play.
options.C: Break the independent play activity down into small chunks so that it can be completed by the student.
options.D: Provide the student with detailed instructions for each specific element of the independent play activity.
